newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: The South African rand staged a minor recovery on Wednesday after early attempts to hurl it through the key 4.50 level failed and calm began to return to the market after Tuesday's blowoff.
At the local close, the currency was pegged at 4.4740/4790 against the dollar from 4.4490/4540 overnight.

At the start of the day, the rand came under attack from players rattled by the rand's eight-cent pummeling on Tuesday in the wake of comments by Reserve Bank Governor Chris Stals that the rand's recent rapid rise could be a slight overadjustment.

But attempts at pushing it through the psychological 4.50 level were thwarted by what dealers said appeared to be Reserve Bank intervention and exporters cashing on an exchange rate last seen when it strengthened from 4.53 to 4.47 on February 5.
The burst of activity proved shortlived, however, and the currency steadily made its way back to the 4.47 area, helped by offshore dollar selling around the 4.48 level.

Dealers said that after digesting Stals' other comments on plans to remove exchange controls on individuals and his upbeat assessment of the balance of payments, the market appeared to be taking a more positive view.

"Initially the market took (Stals' comments) as bearish but if you really look at it logically it is positive...they were good comments which were a good way of showing that things are being done," a senior trader said.
He said that while the market remained jittery after Tuesday's volatility, calm would return in the coming days. Over that time, he said the rand was expected to trade in a 4.45 to 4.50 range.
"It's well protected at 4.50...there is good selling up there so it should hold for now until we get a bit of stability back into the market," he said.
Against the crosses, the rand lost ground against sterling to 7.2240/2333 from 7.1398/1490 overnight, but recovered against the mark to last trade at 0.3770/3774 from 0.3744/3750 marks previously.
Yields on the bond market also retraced from their weakest levels, although dealers said price movements belied what was generally a quiet, jobber-driven day.
The key R150 was last quoted 14.735 percent from 14.715 percent on Tuesday.
Dealers said trade on the day had been generally directionless and the market appeared to be entering a consolidation phase which could last until budget day on March 12.

On the money market, three-month NCDs were quoted higher at between 16.50 percent and 16.70 percent from between 16.45 and 16.65 percent on Tuesday, while the 90-day BA rate was up at between 15.90 and 16.05 percent from 15.80 and 16.05 percent previously.
The Reserve Bank indicated the money market shortage at 10.501 billion rand on Tuesday from 9.993 billion rand on Monday.

Bond Exchange statistics showed foreigners were net sellers of 333.46 million rand's worth of South African bonds on Tuesday after buying 8.31 million rand on Monday. Nominal cumulative turnover was 7.26 billion rand from 4.26 billion rand previously.
